properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — thinking out loud with Anthony, 2026-08-11, from his question "should reflow2 allow something to proceed without a requirement?" Nothing here is intent.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT PROVOKED IT, taken on reflow2's own graph. 148 Capabilities, 18 with zero outgoing SATISFIES:

  16  `imported` BL-nnn backlog rows      none realized   — wishes nobody has built
   1  `authored`, not realized                            — a half-finished thought
   1  `authored`, REALIZED BY AN ARTIFACT                 — cap:governance-proposal: SHIPPED CODE

All eighteen scored 0.55 with the same wording: "satisfies no requirement — what need does it serve, or should it go?" The one instance of shipped-but-unrequested in the entire design is indistinguishable from a parked backlog row.

WHAT THE DETECTOR CURRENTLY GRADES ON (detect.rs:1269-1300): `provenance`. `inferred` → 0.70 with "is built and running, but no requirement justifies it — is there a need nobody wrote down, or is this dead code?"; everything else → 0.55. The docstring is explicit that the bump exists to catch a feature in production during an ADOPTION pass.

⭐ THE OBSERVATION: `provenance` answers "where did this node come from" (recovered from a real system vs written into the design). It does NOT answer "does code exist for this". On the adopt path those coincide, which is why the split works there and was never wrong. On the GENESIS path — a design under control where somebody builds an unrequested feature, which is Anthony's scenario — the capability is `authored` because a person wrote it in deliberately, AND realized because they shipped it. It lands at 0.55 with wording that reads like tidying up an idea.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Add REALIZES-presence as a second axis: authored+realized reads at the higher severity with the "built and running" wording, because the cost of a wrong answer is a maintenance burden rather than a stray node.
(b) Leave severity alone and change only the WORDING when realized, so the reader can tell shipped from unbuilt without the ranking moving.
(c) Do nothing — 0.55 already surfaces it and the reader can look.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside rather than suppressed: the current 0.70/0.55 split was tuned so that `inferred` "clears `unsatisfied_requirement`'s 0.60 default exactly on the graph where the trial wanted it to and nowhere else" (detect.rs:1265-1268). Adding a second way to reach 0.70 changes a threshold that was set against a real trial, and nobody has re-run that trial. Option (b) is the version that costs nothing here.

ALSO UNRESOLVED: no detector reads Project.mode at all (`project_mode` is read in genesis.rs and heal.rs, never in detect.rs). Whether mode SHOULD enter this is a separate question — provenance may already be carrying it adequately.
properties.name: OPEN — should `unmotivated_capability` grade on whether the thing is BUILT, rather than only on provenance?
properties.rationale: Anthony asked whether reflow2 should allow a capability with no requirement. It does, and reports it — but the report cannot distinguish shipped code from a parked wish, which are the two ends of exactly the judgement he was worried about.
